raw_response:
I’m old now, so I don’t like to toss things around too much. This 24 mu is what feeds us, and wheat-maize is what I know best. Last year, the wheat and maize both still did alright if I kept the timing tight and didn’t save too much on fertilizer. People around here mostly do the same. I can pump well water, but that costs money, so I only use it at the important times. With just two people in the house, I also need the work to be simple and on time, especially after wheat harvest when maize has to go in fast. I’ll stay with the usual wheat-maize rotation on all 24 mu, use the seed I trust from the local dealer, put enough fertilizer so the crop doesn’t go hungry, and not gamble on anything fancy.

For wheat, I’ll sow in early October, same as the village does, with a decent base fertilizer and one topdressing when the seedlings start taking off in spring. If winter and spring are dry, I’ll irrigate a few times, but not more than needed because electricity and water both cost money. For maize, I’ll plant right after wheat harvest in June, no delay, and keep the land work simple so I don’t miss the moisture. I’ll use a little more fertilizer on maize too, because if maize lacks feed in summer the yield drops fast. If weeds or insects show up, I’ll spray, but I won’t spend money unless I see a real problem.
